headline_marked: 4 [[warehouses of Salman Muqtadir’s father-in-law sealed]] over alcohol irregularities
headline: 4 warehouses of Salman Muqtadir’s father-in-law sealed over alcohol irregularities
summary: Authorities sealed the facilities in Gulshan after finding duty-free alcohol stored in unauthorized warehouses, amid wider investigations into financial irregularities.
details: Authorities have sealed four warehouses belonging to Sheikh Nur Islam, the father-in-law of content creator Salman Muqtadir, over allegations of storing duty-free alcohol in unauthorized facilities.
The National Board of Revenue (NBR) stated that only two of the four warehouses at Toss Bond Private Limited in South Gulshan were authorized or declared.
The joint operation was conducted by the Customs Intelligence and Investigation Directorate (CIID), the Department of Narcotics Control, and the Special Response Battalion (SRB).
Toss Bond operates as a diplomatic bonded warehouse supplying duty-free alcohol to foreign diplomats, but it has been under scrutiny for allegedly selling goods on the open market.
NBR intelligence units also obtained information from Canada indicating that Nur Islam and his family hold Canadian citizenship and have 'suspicious' transactions in at least four companies.
Financial reports reviewed by agencies covered transactions between 2012 and 2022, with some documents showing remittances of around Tk 9.5 billion in a single year.
While the investigation gained pace after an attack on Salman Muqtadir's studio on Sept 26, officials insist the warehouse sealing is not linked to that specific incident.
The Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit (BFIU) has also sought information regarding Salman Muqtadir's bank accounts.
caption:
4 warehouses sealed in Gulshan! Authorities uncover unauthorized duty-free alcohol storage and suspicious billions in remittances.

Authorities have sealed four warehouses belonging to Sheikh Nur Islam, the father-in-law of content creator Salman Muqtadir, over allegations of storing duty-free alcohol in unauthorized facilities.

The National Board of Revenue (NBR) stated that only two of the four warehouses at Toss Bond Private Limited in South Gulshan were authorized or declared.

The joint operation was conducted by the Customs Intelligence and Investigation Directorate (CIID), the Department of Narcotics Control, and the Special Response Battalion (SRB).

Toss Bond operates as a diplomatic bonded warehouse supplying duty-free alcohol to foreign diplomats, but it has been under scrutiny for allegedly selling goods on the open market.

NBR intelligence units also obtained information from Canada indicating that Nur Islam and his family hold Canadian citizenship and have 'suspicious' transactions in at least four companies.

Financial reports reviewed by agencies covered transactions between 2012 and 2022, with some documents showing remittances of around Tk 9.5 billion in a single year.

While the investigation gained pace after an attack on Salman Muqtadir's studio on Sept 26, officials insist the warehouse sealing is not linked to that specific incident.

The Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit (BFIU) has also sought information regarding Salman Muqtadir's bank accounts.

headline: AQI: Dhaka ranks 5th most polluted among world's cities
summary: The capital city's air quality index continues to be a major health concern as it places high on the global pollution list.
details: Dhaka has been ranked as the 5th most polluted city in the world based on recent Air Quality Index (AQI) data.
The high levels of pollution in the capital city pose significant health risks to millions of residents.
Poor air quality is often attributed to construction dust, vehicle emissions, and industrial pollution in the densely populated urban area.
Environmental experts emphasize the need for urgent measures to tackle the smog and improve the city's breathable air.
